title: Verse or Inspirational Quote?
subtitle: Did Jesus say it, or did Pinterest?

options.explanation: This is NOT in the Bible — it traces back to Aesop's Fables and was later popularized by Benjamin Franklin. Scripture actually teaches the opposite: God helps the helpless (Romans 5:6).
Correct — this is not in the Bible. It's from Aesop's Fables, and Scripture actually emphasizes that God helps the helpless (Romans 5:6).

questions.text: "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me."

options.explanation: Yes — Philippians 4:13. Paul wrote this from prison, in the context of being content in any circumstance.
This is a real verse — Philippians 4:13. Paul wrote it from prison about contentment in any circumstance.

questions.text: "God will never give you more than you can handle."

options.explanation: This is NOT in the Bible. It's a misreading of 1 Corinthians 10:13, which actually says God won't let you be tempted beyond what you can bear — about temptation, not life's hardships.
Correct — not in the Bible. 1 Corinthians 10:13 talks about temptation, not suffering, and 2 Corinthians 1:8 says Paul was burdened beyond his strength so he would rely on God.

questions.text: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life."

options.explanation: Yes — John 3:16. The most-quoted verse in the Bible, spoken by Jesus to Nicodemus.
This is the most famous verse in the Bible — John 3:16, spoken by Jesus to Nicodemus.
This is NOT in the Bible. It comes from a John Wesley sermon in 1778, where he was quoting an even older proverb.
Correct — not in the Bible. It comes from a John Wesley sermon in 1778, quoting an older proverb.

questions.text: "Money is the root of all evil."

options.explanation: MISQUOTE — 1 Timothy 6:10 actually says "the LOVE of money is the root of ALL KINDS of evil." Money itself isn't the root; loving it is.
Correct — this is a misquote. 1 Timothy 6:10 says "the LOVE of money is the root of all KINDS of evil." Money itself isn't condemned; loving it is.

questions.text: "Be still, and know that I am God."

options.explanation: Yes — Psalm 46:10. A call to stop striving and recognize God's sovereignty over the nations.
This is Psalm 46:10 — a call to stop striving and recognize God's sovereignty.
This is NOT in the Bible. It comes from a Persian fable, popularized in the West by Abraham Lincoln.
Correct — not in the Bible. It's from a medieval Persian fable, later popularized in English by Abraham Lincoln.
This is NOT in the Bible. It comes from a 1773 hymn by William Cowper: "God moves in a mysterious way, His wonders to perform." Isaiah 55:8-9 captures a similar idea biblically.
Correct — not in the Bible. It's from an 18th-century hymn by William Cowper. Isaiah 55:8-9 captures a similar idea in actual Scripture.

questions.text: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding."

options.explanation: Yes — Proverbs 3:5, one of the most beloved verses in the wisdom literature.
This is Proverbs 3:5 — one of the most beloved verses in the wisdom literature.
